findings.title: Fallback locales are only loaded in controller requests; jobs, mailers and with_locale blocks get no fallback
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` is called only from `ApplicationController#set_locale` (application_controller.rb:159). Other paths set the locale without it: `I18n.with_locale(user.effective_locale)` in app/services/post_alerter.rb:138, `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale` in app/jobs/base.rb:151, and `I18n.with_locale` in lib/post_destroyer.rb:102. The accelerator's `translate` loads only `config.locale` (translate_accelerator.rb:68). In those paths the fallback chain (site default, `:en`) can name a locale whose yml was never loaded in the process. This is most likely in a Sidekiq process, which serves no controller requests. A key missing in the user's locale then gives 'translation missing' instead of the fallback text. This is the case fallbacks are meant to cover, for example in notification emails. Because `translate` caches by `key+locale+backend` (line 72), the missing-string result is also cached. A later request with the fallback loaded still gets the stale string. Load the fallback chain inside the accelerated `translate`/`load_locale` path (for example, load every `I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]` locale there) instead of only in the controller filter.

findings.title: LRU cache key ignores the fallback chain
findings.body: The cache key is `key + config.locale + backend.object_id`. With fallbacks, the result now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which `FallbackLocaleList#[]` reads (i18n.rb:17), and on which fallback locales are loaded. If an admin changes the default locale, or a lookup is cached before the fallback locale is loaded, the cache keeps serving the old result until `reload!` runs. Include the fallback chain in the key, or clear `@cache` when `default_locale` changes.

findings.title: No tests for the fallback behaviour
findings.body: The change adds fallback ordering (user locale, site locale, en), `ensure_loaded!`, and enabling fallbacks in the development and test environments. It adds no spec. spec/controllers/application_controller_spec.rb already has a `set_locale` describe block, so a spec for a key missing in the user locale resolving to the site locale and then to en would fit there. A spec for `I18n.ensure_loaded!` would also be useful.

findings.title: Initializer ordering depends on an implicit filename sort
findings.body: The comment says `# order: after 02-freedom_patches.rb`, and the file is named `i18n.rb`. It only runs after the freedom patches because Rails loads initializers alphabetically and digits sort before letters. The comment explains this poorly. A `NN-` prefix, such as `03-i18n.rb`, would make the ordering explicit and consistent with the other numbered initializers.

contracts.action: Enable I18n fallbacks (user locale, site default locale, en) in all environments via a custom FallbackLocaleList, replacing config.i18n.fallbacks = true in production and profile
contracts.equivalent_path: Rails' `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` in production.rb, profile.rb and the cloud66 production.rb. It used I18n::Locale::Fallbacks with defaults [default_locale].
contracts.before_after: Before, fallbacks applied only in production and profile, and only fell back to I18n.default_locale. After, they apply in every environment, with a chain of locale, SiteSetting.default_locale and :en, computed per lookup.
contracts.visible_effect: Missing strings in a user's locale show the site-locale or English text instead of 'translation missing'.
contracts.failure_mode: The fallback locales' yml is loaded only in ApplicationController#set_locale. Jobs, mailers and with_locale blocks never load it. A fallback lookup there can return 'translation missing', which the LRU cache then keeps.

contracts.action: I18n.ensure_loaded!(locale) added to the translate accelerator
contracts.equivalent_path: I18n.load_locale, called lazily from `translate` for config.locale only
contracts.before_after: Before, only config.locale was loaded on demand. After, the controller also loads each fallback locale. load_locale is mutex-guarded and returns early if the locale is already loaded, so repeated calls are cheap.
contracts.visible_effect: Fallback strings are available on web requests.
contracts.failure_mode: The `@loaded_locales ||= []` initialisation sits outside LOAD_MUTEX. That is harmless because reload! and load_locale also initialise it.

summary: The change moves fallbacks into a custom initializer with a user-locale, site-locale, en chain, and loads those locales on web requests. Fallback locales are not loaded outside controller requests, so jobs, mailers and `with_locale` blocks may get 'translation missing'. The LRU translation cache key also ignores the fallback chain. No tests were added. I did not run anything.
